outcome.summary: Adopted the Staff-Georgia Power stipulation: IRP approved as amended, with 26% winter/20% summer reserve margins, authority to seek certification of up to 8,500 MW in the 2029-2031 all-source RFP, extended operation of Scherer Unit 3 and Gaston, Vogtle uprates approved and Hatch uprates and Goat Rock capacity not approved at this time. Denied GIPL and Southface's motion to enforce the Vogtle settlement.

notes: Docket 56002 was heard jointly with DSM Docket 56003; one stipulation and one order cover both, so DSM asks appear where they were a party's main request. Positions use each party's post-hearing brief except: PIA Staff (cites its July 9 stipulation filing; that filing's stipulation pages have no text, so terms were read from the GPC-filed version, doc 223329); CEBA (its July 10 Clarification and Proposed Commissioner Motions, filed after the stipulation); and parties that signed the stipulation later (APA, SREA, GAM, GSEIA, DOD/FEA, Walmart via doc 223329; Capital Good Fund via doc 223391). APA and SREA filed one joint brief but signed the stipulation separately, so each has its own entry. Capital Good Fund's signature does not appear in the text layer of doc 223391; its joinder rests on the filing title and the July 31 order, p. 9. Stance for stipulation signatories is 'supports with changes' because the stipulation amends the filed plan (e.g., Hatch uprates and Goat Rock capacity not approved; additional sums cut from $4.00 to $3.00/kW and $3.50/kW-yr). Staff's July 3 brief and proposed order, before the stipulation, had sought a 24.5% winter reserve margin, modified large load materialization assumptions, a 6,000 MW certification limit (with up to 2,000 MW more on rate base conditions), and a two-year delay of the Hatch uprates. GIPL/Southface stance is a judgment call: they oppose the load forecast lock-in but back the Company's 0.75% DSM savings target at a lower budget. On July 10, 2025 they also moved to enforce the Vogtle settlement (strike stipulation DSM paras. 5, 8, 9); the July 31 order denied it. Their separate trade secret challenge was decided Sept 4, 2025 (order text not available). Georgia Conservation Voters filed the Roumpani testimony under that name; the brief was filed as Georgia Conservation Voters Education Fund, treated as one party. Parties without a stated position: Resource Supply Management filed an interim and final brief, and Georgia Center for Energy Solutions filed testimony (Peter Hubbard), but no text is available for either. Concerned Ratepayers of Georgia filed public-witness-format testimony (no text). Fermata, MARTA, AACE, Georgia Watch and Microsoft filed only intervention or appearance papers. The July 31 order records the Commission vote in Administrative Session on July 15, 2025. Later items in this docket not covered: Sept 30, 2025 DCO-1/LCOR-1 tariff filing; April 22, 2026 order approving the Renewable Integration Cost Update; Oct 9, 2026 order approving the 2026 Plant Hatch 1-2 extended power uprates; plus compliance reports (hydro, nuclear uprate, 111 GHG, ECS, DERMS, transmission).
